priceSnapshot.note: The morning session's add trigger fired, and it fired exactly the way the morning session said it had to. The condition was a settled 1H close above $65,000 WITH open interest flat or rising across the same bar. The 13:00Z hour did both at once: it opened at 64,952.6, ran to 65,259.0, and settled at 65,219.9 - a 267-point range and the largest hourly expansion of the week - while open interest rose. Price then extended to 65,300.0 on the 14:00Z bar, which is the session and 24-hour high, and has spent the three hours since holding a tight 65,146.8 to 65,268.1 shelf. Against the morning reference at 64,961.3 spot is up 253.6 points, 0.390%, in five hours fifty-two minutes. Against the midnight stamp of 64,852.0 it is up 362.9 points, 0.560%. What has NOT happened matters as much: 65,300.0 is still 88.0 points below the 07 August high of 65,388.0 and 108.8 below the 31 July high of 65,423.7. The multi-week range top has not been touched, let alone broken. This is a trigger break inside a range, not a range breakout.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $64,650 - held UNCHANGED for a TENTH consecutive session and now further from price than at any point in the ten. Spot 65,214.9 gives 564.9 points of clearance, 0.87%, which is 0.40 of a daily ATR. The line stays where it is because everything that justified it is still underneath it and has now been reinforced by the move: the daily EMA50 at 64,695.5, the 1H EMA100 at 64,739.9, the 64,750 realized-liquidation shelf, the 4H EMA20 at 64,841.5, the 15m EMA200 at 64,919.2 and this session's 64,913.0 low all sit between price and the trigger. A settled hourly close beneath 64,650 would require unwinding six separate levels in sequence and would end the higher-low structure that has run unbroken since the 64,722.7 print at 03:00Z.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $65,300, WITH open interest holding or rising across the same bar. The trigger is RAISED 300 points from the morning's 65,000 because 65,000 has been paid: the 13:00Z bar settled at 65,219.9 and price has not traded below 64,913.0 since. 65,300.0 is the honest next test - it is this session's high, it is the 24-hour high, it is the top of the $447,017 short-liquidation cluster that produced the whole move, and it is the last obstacle before the 65,388.0 range top set on 07 August. The open-interest condition is retained verbatim from the morning session because it is the rule that has now worked twice: it correctly rejected the 08 August 65,120 break, which came on FALLING open interest and failed, and it correctly confirmed this one, which came on open interest rising 3.62%.

decisionBox.changed: Position stays ADD for a third consecutive session, but the character of the add has changed from confirming a break to sizing into one that has already run. The morning deployed 10 USDT at 64,961.3 on a half-fired signal and named the condition for the remaining 12.38 precisely: a settled close above 65,000 or a retest of the 64,784.9 session low. The first of those has fired. The reason this session deploys only 5 of the 12.38 rather than all of it is that the tape has changed underneath the trigger in one specific way - the 15m MACD histogram has flipped from +16.21 at the morning read to -11.03 now, while price rose 253.6 points, which is a fresh short-frame bearish divergence and marks the 65,300.0 print as the momentum peak rather than a launch point. The reduce line is untouched at 64,650 for a tenth session; the add trigger is raised to 65,300.

liquidation.note: This is the story of the session and it is a new cluster that did not exist at the morning read. Bucketing all 186 fills returned by OKX /public/liquidation-orders over the 2026-08-08T18:51:19Z to 2026-08-09T16:57:43Z window into 250-USD bands - BTC-USDT-SWAP contract multiplier 0.01 BTC - the 65,250 band carries $447,017 of the $779,027 total across 93 separate fills. That is 57.4% of everything liquidated in 22 hours 6 minutes concentrated in one 250-point pocket, and the composition is close to one-sided: $435,932 SHORT against $11,085 long, a 39:1 ratio. Shorts positioned for the range top to hold were carried out en masse on the 13:00Z and 14:00Z bars, and that forced buying IS the move. The reason it is flagged magnet rather than support is that a cluster this lopsided is spent fuel once it has burned - the squeeze that produced 65,300.0 has already consumed the shorts that were sitting there. Fresh shorts are arriving to replace them, which the long/short account ratio confirms, but they are being added ABOVE the level rather than trapped beneath it.

The pocket the morning session named as its add trigger, now sitting 214.9 points beneath spot and converted from resistance into the first genuine shelf. It carries $69,677 across 18 fills, $59,463 of it short against $10,214 long. It is small in dollar terms next to the other two bands, but its value is confluence rather than size: the round number, the 15m EMA100 at 65,012.7 and the 1H EMA20 at 65,038.6 all sit inside a 40-point window here. This is where a pullback should first be bought and it is where the wallet's remaining 7.38 USDT of dry powder is aimed.

The shelf that has defined the week, unchanged in size from the morning read at $262,332 across 75 fills, $144,167 short against $118,165 long. It has now been left 464.9 points behind and no new fills have printed there since the morning session, which is the clearest possible evidence that it did its job. It stays on the map as the structural floor: it sits directly on top of the 1H EMA100 at 64,739.9 and immediately above the daily EMA50 at 64,695.5 and the 64,650 reduce trigger. If the 65,000 shelf fails, this is the next place the desk expects a real bid rather than a bounce.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull is up but it is a weaker up than the raw numbers suggest, and the distinction is the most important judgement in this report. The largest cluster by far is above at 65,250 and unfinished business normally drags price toward it. What tempers that reading is that price has ALREADY been through it - the 65,300.0 print consumed the cluster rather than being drawn into it, so what remains above is not a pool of trapped shorts but the memory of one. The genuinely forward-looking signal is elsewhere: the OKX long/short ACCOUNT ratio FELL from 1.21 at the morning read to 1.13 on the 17:00Z bucket while price rose 0.39% and open interest rose 3.62%. Falling account ratio with rising open interest and rising price means the new positioning arriving is disproportionately SHORT. Traders are fading this move. That is fuel above 65,300 rather than exhaustion, and it is why the add trigger sits there rather than being abandoned.

divergences.note: Price rose 253.6 points between the morning read and this one while the 15m MACD histogram fell from +16.21 to -11.03, crossing below zero on the way. Higher price against a lower and now-negative oscillator is a textbook bearish divergence, and it is the single argument against sizing this session's add fully. It replaces the 4H divergence the morning session flagged, which has RESOLVED - that histogram recovered from -37.31 to -10.47 over the same window, so the warning has migrated from the intermediate frame to the short one. Two qualifications keep it from dominating. First, it is a histogram divergence on a 15-minute chart across a three-hour consolidation that followed a 267-point impulse bar; a pause after that kind of move produces this signature almost mechanically. Second, the 15m EMA stack is in perfect bullish order beneath price, so the structure has not deteriorated at all - only the rate of change has. Treated as a size constraint, which is exactly how the morning session treated the 4H version, and that call scored correctly.

calibration.rollingRecord: 60 rows on file before this one. The 09 Aug morning session called range with a bullish tilt at 40/44/16 from 64,961.3, held position at ADD, held the reduce at 64,650 for a ninth session, RAISED the add trigger from 64,920 to 65,000 with an explicit open-interest condition attached, and deployed 10 of 22.38 USDT of free cash into spot. Every one of those five decisions has scored correctly, and two of them scored emphatically. The bullish tilt was right: price is 65,214.9, up 253.6 points or 0.390%, the largest gain across any single inter-session window this week. Holding 64,650 was right and was never remotely tested - the lowest trade since is 64,913.0, so the line kept 263 points of clearance at its closest. The 65,000 add trigger was the best-placed level of the day: it was set 38.7 points above the then-spot, price took two hours to reach it, and the 13:00Z bar settled at 65,219.9 to fire it with 219.9 points to spare. The open-interest condition attached to that trigger is the decision that deserves the credit, because it is what separated this break from the 08 August failure - it demanded participation and got 3.62%. And the 10 USDT tranche is in profit: bought at a 64,961.3 mark, worth 10.039 at 65,214.9. The morning's ONE miss is a scoring artifact rather than a judgement error - its calibration row was written at 06:59 COT with add_fired=false, and the trigger fired six hours later at 13:00Z. That row is left untouched here under the merge rule; the endday session should backfill it to true along with price_next_report.
calibration.note: The reduce level at 64,650 has now survived TEN consecutive sessions without a settled hourly close beneath it, and for the second session running it was not tested at all. The open question the desk has carried since 08 August is closed for now: a break through a trigger is worth sizing when open interest expands into it and worth fading when it contracts, and the rule has now been tested twice in both directions and been right both times. The new open question replaces it and is sharper. The long/short account ratio FELL from 1.21 to 1.13 while price rose and open interest rose 3.62%, which means the incremental positioning is short. That is bullish fuel if 65,300 gives way and it is a crowd that will be proved right if it does not. The endday session inherits the test.
